Huang and Yang (2016) expanded DBH–height models for Alberta tree species

Source: R/hd_huang2016b.R
hd_huang2016b.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the population-level expanded individual-tree height–diameter models in Huang and Yang (2016; Alberta Tech. Rep. T/610). Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm), the basal area (m²/ha) and the mean height of the dominant and co-dominant trees (m) of the tree's species.

Usage

hd_huang2016b(DBH, species, HDOM, BA, keep_model_id = FALSE)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PICE.GLA"; compact "PICEGLA" is accepted), or one of "DECID", "CONIF", "ALL" for the source's combined models.

HDOM

Numeric vector. Plot level. Mean height (m) of all the dominant and co-dominant trees with measured heights in the plot, computed for the tree's species (source group, Table 1), or for all deciduous, all conifer or all trees with "DECID", "CONIF" or "ALL" (source symbol \(H_{DC}\); Section 6.2). Must be > 0.

BA

Numeric vector. Plot level. Basal area (m²/ha) of the trees taller than 1.3 m of the tree's species (source group, Table 1), or of all deciduous, all conifer or all trees with "DECID", "CONIF" or "ALL" (Section 6.1). Must be >= 0.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("huang2016b").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope (species coverage): aspen (POPU.TRE), balsam poplar (POPU.BAL), white birch (BETU.PAP), lodgepole pine (PINU.CON), white spruce (PICE.GLA), black spruce (PICE.MAR), Douglas-fir (PSEU.MEN), tamarack (LARI.LAR) and jack pine (PINU.BAN). Following the source species grouping (Table 1), whitebark pine (PINU.ALB) and limber pine (PINU.FLE) use the lodgepole pine equation, Engelmann spruce (PICE.ENG) uses white spruce, and western (LARI.OCC) and alpine larch (LARI.LYA) use tamarack; a one-time message reports the mapping. The source's combined models are selected with species = "DECID" (all deciduous species), "CONIF" (all conifers) or "ALL" (all species combined).

Balsam fir is not available: in the source, the balsam fir base coefficients (Table A1, part 2) are an exact copy of the black spruce column, while the fit statistics in Table 5 show a different balsam fir model. Balsam fir (ABIE.BAL) and subalpine fir (ABIE.LAS, grouped with balsam fir) therefore raise an error.

Model forms: deciduous species and "DECID" use eq. [1], $$H = 1.3 + (b_1 + b_2 BA + b_3 HDOM) [1 - \exp(-b_4 DBH)]^{b_5};$$ conifers, "CONIF" and "ALL" use eq. [2], $$H = 1.3 + (b_1 + b_2 BA + b_3 HDOM) / (1 + \exp[b_4 + b_5 \ln(DBH + 0.01)]).$$

Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured at 1.3 m, so predicted height tends to 1.3 m as DBH tends to 0.

Population-level prediction: coefficients are those of the base (fixed-effects) models in Table A1, which the source recommends for trees in plots without height measurements (Section 5). Plot-specific calibration with the mixed models is not implemented.

Rows with NA in any input return NA height. DBH, BA or HDOM values outside the range of the fitting data of the species (Table 2) are computed and reported in a single warning.

References

Huang, S., and Yang, Y. (2016). Expanded individual tree height prediction models from tree diameter and other variables. Report #5, Tech. Rep. Pub. No. T/610. Forestry Division, Alberta Agriculture and Forestry, Edmonton, Alberta.

See also

hd_huang2016() for the DBH-only models of the same report series; hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

# Aspen worked example (T/610 Table 6, plot 1)
hd_huang2016b(DBH = c(29.7, 1.6), species = "POPU.TRE",
              HDOM = 29.9333, BA = 36.8225)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1  27.2 
#> 2   3.14

trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(12, 25, 40),
  species = c("PICE.MAR", "PICE.GLA", "PINU.CON"),
  HDOM = c(15, 24, 20),
  BA = c(20, 25, 34)
)
dplyr::mutate(trees, hd_huang2016b(DBH, species, HDOM, BA))
#>   DBH  species HDOM BA   height
#> 1  12 PICE.MAR   15 20 12.18090
#> 2  25 PICE.GLA   24 25 21.93206
#> 3  40 PINU.CON   20 34 22.51643

# Combined conifer model (HDOM and BA of all conifers)
hd_huang2016b(DBH = 30, species = "CONIF", HDOM = 21, BA = 37)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   23.2
